title: Security review kickoff: Merrow Vale Water
scratchpad:
Hollis (IT security) - ~60 question questionnaire
wants SSO, 90d location ok, no customer-managed keys (told him)
answers back by end Nov (insurer renews Jan)
Elena owns, Odette for technical
segments: Hollis, thanks for joining. This is the first security conversation, so it's mostly us learning what your review looks like.
Happy to. We're a small water board, but our insurer has started asking hard questions about every vendor that touches customer data.
The formal part is a questionnaire, about sixty questions. I'll send it over after this call. Most of it is standard.
What matters most to you in it, so we know where to spend our time?
Three things: who can log in and how, how long you keep our data, and what you log.
Logins first, then. Single sign-on through SAML, and we can switch off password logins for your whole organisation.
Good. We use our own identity provider for everything, so that's a must for us.
And multi-factor for anyone at Quillmark who can see our data?
Everyone with production access uses hardware keys. No exceptions, including me.
And background checks? The insurer has a question about staff screening that I never know how to answer for vendors.
Everyone with production access is background checked before they start. I can describe the process in the questionnaire, without any personal details.
Retention. We'd like work orders kept while the contract runs, and location data kept for as short a time as possible.
Location breadcrumbs are on a rolling ninety days by default, and we can shorten that per customer. Work orders stay while the contract is active.
Ninety days is fine for us, actually. Our crews are small and they're used to it, so it's less sensitive for us than it might be elsewhere.
Encryption. Our insurer specifically asks whether we can hold our own encryption keys.
Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Customer managed keys aren't something we offer today, and I'd rather be straight with you about that.
That's fine. I'll write it down as not available. The insurer cares more that we asked than about the answer.
Logging. What do you keep, and can we get it out?
Sign-ins, failed sign-ins, permission changes, exports and every edit to a work order. One year in the admin console, or we can stream it to a system of yours.
We don't have a system to stream into, honestly. One year in your console is plenty for an organisation our size.
What about backups? If something goes wrong on your side, how far back can you restore our data?
Backups run continuously, and we test a full restore every quarter. I'll put the details in the encryption and backup section.
And if your insurer has follow-up questions after reading the answers, we're happy to get on a call with them directly.
What's the timeline on your side? When do you need the answers back?
Our insurer renews in January, so I'd like the questionnaire back by the end of November. Earlier is better, if you can.
I'll own the questionnaire on our side and pull Odette in for the technical answers. You'll have it well before the end of November.
Perfect. One more thing: do you carry cyber insurance yourselves? They'll ask about that too.
We do. I'll include a summary of our policy with the questionnaire.
Great. That covers my list. I'll send the questionnaire this afternoon.
Thanks, Hollis. We're looking forward to working through it with you.

items.text: Return Merrow Vale's security questionnaire, with Odette's technical answers, before the end of November
Merrow Vale's questionnaire has about sixty questions
Merrow Vale asked for customer-managed encryption keys; not offered today
